goal: The pixel-perfect landing page — say what it is, show it working, and get visitors installed — built with pixel-perfect so the site, its Storybook, and its inventory are the proof.
vibe: Press proof — a printer's proof sheet. The four process inks (cyan, magenta, yellow, black) on cool neutral paper; overlaps multiply in light mode and screen in dark mode; magenta is the only accent for action and emphasis, and yellow is never body or interface text (it appears only in decorative plate copies and code-panel syntax). Anybody for display, Libre Franklin for body, IBM Plex Mono for code and labels. Crop marks, registration targets, a color control strip, slug lines, and numbered proofreader marks, each meaning something. Both themes designed deliberately; WCAG 2.2 AA; CSS-only motion that honors reduced motion.

motion.why_recorded: The frame renderer captures still frames with reduced motion forced, so the inventory and every golden show only end states. This block is the only durable record of what moves. The other three exports have no motion.
motion.spec: Strategy §10.4: two orchestrated moments on load; CSS only; never hijacks scrolling; off for visitors who set reduce motion. The design adds five scroll-driven moments beyond those two.
motion.reduced_motion: When prefers-reduced-motion is reduce, every animation and transition is off and scroll progress is never computed, so each element renders its end state (listed per entry as end_state). Design lines 36 and 437.

scroll_progress.what: Reference behaviour from the design: each scroll-driven element has a progress p from 0 to 1 as it crosses the viewport, and its styles are functions of p. The build reproduces p with a CSS view timeline (see mechanism).
scroll_progress.design_mechanism: The design computes p with a passive scroll listener (design lines 432-456). The build does not port it.
scroll_progress.css_mapping: p = 0 when the element's top is at start x viewport height and p = 1 when it is at end x viewport height, which is animation-range: cover (1 - start) x 100vh cover (1 - end) x 100vh. With span, p = 1 when the element's bottom reaches end x viewport height, which is animation-timeline: view(block (end x 100vh) ((1 - start) x 100vh)) with animation-range: cover 0% cover 100%.

mechanism.choice: CSS scroll-driven animations: a view timeline and animation-range per element, keyframes declared in @theme, no scroll listener and no script.
mechanism.reason: Matches strategy §10.4 (CSS only), adds no JavaScript, and keeps every motion rule in markup and app.css, where the styling gate can see it.
mechanism.fallback: Where animation-timeline is unsupported, or reduced motion is on, the element renders its end_state. No content depends on motion.
mechanism.rejected: Porting the design's scroll listener: exact on every browser, but it adds a script and moves motion logic out of the styling gate's view.
mechanism.proof: 2026-09-29, headless Chrome 154: CSS view timelines using the css_mapping above reproduced the design's scroll formula exactly (max error 0.0000 over 17 mid-animation samples, covering non-span, span, and two element heights). A deliberately wrong range erred by 0.18, so the check can fail.

load.behavior: Three aria-hidden colour copies of the headline (cyan, magenta, yellow, blended with --blend) start offset and slide into registration by 65% of the run, then fade out while the ink text fades in over them.
load.timing: 1.7s cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.1,1), delay .25s, fill both; keyframes pp-plate and pp-ink
load.end_state: Ink headline only; the colour copies are invisible.

load.behavior: The stack starts as one flat mockup and tilts into the isometric view (rotateX 58deg, rotateZ -32deg) as its five layers lift to their depths.
load.timing: 1.8s cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1), delay .5s, fill both; keyframe pp-flat
load.end_state: Tilted stack with layers at their resting depths.
load.note: Fig. 1 is hidden at 720px and below; the proof slider replaces it on mobile.

scroll.element: Fig. 1 layer stack and its layer labels
scroll.behavior: The four upper layers spread apart in depth as you scroll: translateZ(10+14p, 20+28p, 30+42p, 40+56p px). The label list (Screens to Tokens) opens its gap from 8px to 24px in step.

scroll.element: Drifted card and its four proofreader marks
scroll.behavior: The drifted card visibly drifts (corner radius 4 to 5px, padding 16 to 20px), and proofreader marks 1 to 4 pop in one by one (opacity 0 to 1, scale .5 to 1) at p = .25, .40, .55, .70.
scroll.end_state: p = 1: fully drifted card with all four marks shown.

scroll.element: Four-step list and its progress rail
scroll.behavior: A magenta rail fills top to bottom (height p x 100%) while each step brightens from 50% to full opacity as the rail reaches it (steps 1 to 4 at p = -.10, .20, .45, .70, each over 0.1 of progress).
scroll.end_state: p = 1: rail full, all four steps at full opacity.

scroll.element: The evolve result: a new Changelog page
scroll.behavior: The Changelog page's five parts fly in from scattered offsets and settle into place (translate by (1-p) x offset, opacity .3 to 1), showing a new page assembled from existing parts.
The same plate effect as the hero, driven by scroll: three aria-hidden colour copies converge into registration and fade out (translate by (1-p) x offset, opacity 1-p).
scroll.end_state: p = 1: ink headline only, in registration.

motion.accessibility: Colour-plate copies are decorative duplicates and stay aria-hidden; the ink span is the only text a screen reader reads. No content depends on motion (strategy §10.5).
build_notes: Tailwind v4 has no animation-timeline utilities: use arbitrary properties such as [animation-timeline:view()] and [animation-range:cover_10vh_cover_65vh], with each animation's keyframes declared in @theme as --animate-*.
Apply scroll animations only under motion-safe: and supports-[animation-timeline:view()]:, so the base classes are the end_state.

Thresholds inside an element (proofreader marks at p = .25 to .70, build steps, grow parts) become keyframe percentages within that element's animation; for example mark 1 fades and scales in from 25% to 37.5%.
Plate offsets (--dx, --dy and the per-part offsets) are fixed values: set them with arbitrary-property utilities such as [--dx:-16px]. The styling contract bans static inline styles.

fig1-tilt animates the transform property from none. Tailwind v4 translate-z utilities write the separate translate property, which that keyframe does not reset, so keep the layer depths on transform ([transform:translateZ(...)]) or change the keyframe to match.
motion.verify: Each scroll-driven component takes an optional progress prop (0 to 1). When set, it pauses the animation at that point (paused play-state with a negative delay on a 1s duration), so stories capture p = 0 and the end state and Storybook can scrub the motion. Load animations are checked with reduced motion off and on.

tokens.source: ../design/pixel-perfect Landing.dc.html lines 23-24 ([data-pp-root] custom properties); literals elsewhere in the file are promoted below so the styling contract's colour check can pass.

code.note: Code and terminal panels are dark in both themes.

drift.note: The drifted card's deliberately off-system gray in the Why section. It is a named token so the example can show drift without breaking the colour rule; nothing else may use it.

typography.loading: Self-hosted @font-face in src/app.css (the styling contract's only allowed font mechanism), for example from Fontsource variable packages, keeping Anybody's wdth axis. Load only the weights above. Storybook's preview imports app.css so stories use the same faces.
typography.note: logo.js specifies Anybody 800 at wdth 112 for the wordmark while Logo.dc.html renders 700 at 105%; the site header follows the landing export.

layout.breakpoint_note: The design switches layout at 720px, not Tailwind's default 768px: set --breakpoint-md: 720px in @theme.

theme.default: system: follows prefers-color-scheme, light when unknown
theme.toggle: The header button switches light/dark and saves the choice in localStorage.
theme.attribute: data-theme on <html>, set by a small inline script in src/app.html before first paint only when the visitor has saved a choice. Without one, color-scheme: light dark follows prefers-color-scheme, including when JavaScript is off.
theme.tailwind: @custom-variant dark (&:where([data-theme=dark], [data-theme=dark] *)); the colour tokens switch under [data-theme=dark].
theme.storybook: A toolbar global sets data-theme on the preview root; goldens are captured in both themes.
theme.design_note: The export keeps data-theme on an inner [data-pp-root] div with a light body behind it; the build moves it to <html> so the whole page switches.

ui_states.source: Designed 2026-09-29 with the frontend-design skill, in place of redrawing in Claude Design. Extends ../design/pixel-perfect Landing.dc.html: states the export already defines point at its lines; states it never defined are designed here.
ui_states.principle: States reuse the page's print devices. Registration (alignment) marks focus, magenta-ink is the only action colour, mono labels carry status, and no state depends on motion or on colour alone.

contrast.method: WCAG 2.2 relative luminance, computed 2026-09-29. Focus indicators need 3:1 against the surface around them (1.4.11); text needs 4.5:1.
contrast.focus_on_code_panel: #FF7AB9 on code-bg 7.48 (light-theme magenta-ink would be 2.68, so code panels use code-focus)

focus.status: designed here (the export has no focus styles)
focus.applies_to: every link, button, tab, FAQ summary, the theme toggle, the slider, and the focusable tab panel
focus.style: Keyboard focus only (:focus-visible). A 2px solid magenta-ink outline 3px outside the element, square to its corners. Block controls (buttons, tabs, toggle, FAQ summary) also cast a flat cyan plate 3px down-left (box-shadow -3px 3px 0 0 cyan), so a focused control reads as two plates slightly out of register: the plate being checked. Inline text links get the outline only. On code panels the outline uses code-focus and there is no cyan plate, because cyan is a syntax colour there.
focus.tailwind: focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-3 focus-visible:outline-magenta-ink focus-visible:shadow-[-3px_3px_0_0_var(--cyan)]; on code panels focus-visible:outline-code-focus focus-visible:shadow-none

hover.status: designed here (the export only turns links ink)
rules: Primary button (ink): background becomes magenta-ink, text paper. The action colour appears on intent.
Secondary button (outline): border goes from line to ink; background sheet.
Copy button on a code panel: border goes from code-control-border to code-fg.
Nav link: a 2px magenta underline 6px below the text, like a registration rule; text stays ink.
Text link: keeps the export's rule (magenta to ink).
Tab: text goes from muted to ink.
FAQ summary: the + glyph turns magenta-ink.
Theme toggle: border goes from line to ink.
hover.devices: Hover styles apply only where hover exists (Tailwind v4's hover variant already wraps @media (hover: hover)), so touch devices never get stuck hover states.

install_tabs.status: in the export: tab data at Landing:420-427, panel template at Landing:362-370
install_tabs.panels: Each tab shows its numbered command rows. A note (Cursor: 'Then reload the window.', Grok: enable it in /plugins) is a plain 15px line. A warning (Codex duplicate installs, Cursor symlinks) is a 14px line led by a mono magenta-ink 'Note' label. OpenCode and Pi have neither; Claude Code has neither.
install_tabs.keyboard: In the export: arrow keys, Home, and End move between tabs; the selected tab is the only one in the tab order; the hash updates so a tab can be linked.

faq_open.style: Open: the mono glyph changes from + to a minus sign (U+2212) and from muted to magenta-ink. The answer appears instantly under the question (native details); several can be open.
faq_open.tailwind: details.group; + visible with group-open:hidden, minus hidden until group-open:inline, colour group-open:text-magenta-ink
faq_open.a11y: Native details/summary announces expanded and collapsed; the glyph is aria-hidden.

copy.status: labels in the export (Landing:474); layout and announcement designed here; the next step is always shown (decided at B-inv)
copy.labels: Copy, then 'Copied ✓' for 2 seconds. If the clipboard is blocked, the command text is selected instead and the label reads 'Selected'.
copy.layout: The button is as wide as its label, as the design draws it ('Copy'). While 'Copied ✓' or 'Selected' shows (2 seconds) it widens and the command may re-wrap. Decided 2026-09-30 by the owner: the earlier rule (keep the widest label's width, min-width 9ch) made the built card differ from the design, which the hero's real proof pair exposed.
copy.announce: A visually hidden aria-live=polite region per copy block says 'Copied to clipboard' or 'Command selected. Press Command-C or Control-C to copy.'
copy.next_step: Decided at build B-inv: the 'Next: open a project that has your design and run /pixel-perfect:init' line is always shown under the Install tabs in body type, as the export draws it. It is not revealed by copying and does not appear under the hero.

slider.status: behaviour in the export (Landing:123-147); ends, focus, and labels designed here
slider.ends: At 0 the built component fills the pane; at 100 the design frame fills it. The divider sits on the edge, and the handle is clamped so its whole 28px circle stays inside the pane.
slider.keyboard: Native range keys: arrows move 1, Page Up and Page Down move 10, Home and End jump to 0 and 100.
slider.focus: The range input is invisible, so its keyboard focus is drawn on the handle (peer-focus-visible), using the focus style above.
slider.a11y: aria-valuetext reads '{split}% design frame, {100 - split}% built component'.
slider.touch: The pane sets touch-action: pan-y, so a vertical swipe still scrolls the page on phones.

theme_toggle.status: label in the export (Landing:55, 495); names and mobile form designed here
theme_toggle.label: The button names the theme it switches to: 'Dark' with a dark dot in the light theme, 'Light' with a light dot in the dark theme (the dot is the current ink).
theme_toggle.a11y: aria-label 'Switch to dark theme' or 'Switch to light theme'.
theme_toggle.mobile: At 720px and below the button is the dot alone in a 40x40 square; the word is visually hidden.

mobile_header.status: designed here (at 720px and below the export hides the nav with no replacement)
mobile_header.row_1: Sticky, 60px: the logo lockup (mark A and wordmark), then 'Install' as a mono 13px magenta-ink link to #install, then the icon-only theme toggle. Width at 390px: estimated at about 330px of the 358px available; confirm when the header is built.
mobile_header.row_2: Not sticky, directly under the header at the top of the page: a section strip styled as a printer's slug line. Mono caps 11px, letter-spacing .06em, muted, items 'WHY · BUILD IT · GROW IT · INSTALL · FAQ · GITHUB ↗'. It scrolls sideways if it overflows (no visible scrollbar), each link has a 44px tall touch target, and a 1px line sits under it.
mobile_header.why: It reuses the slug-line device the page already has and needs no drawer, no script, and no focus trap. The Install link stays in the sticky row because installing is the page's primary action.

social_card.status: layout from ../design/Social preview.dc.html; lockup changed by the logo decision (strategy D5)
social_card.build: The SocialCard organism is 1200x630, light theme only, and is rendered to og.png at build.
social_card.change: The crosshair and mono 'pixel-perfect' lockup become the site's Logo atom: mark A (stacked plates) with the Anybody wordmark, as in the header. Everything else keeps the export's layout: crop marks, the plate-misregistered headline, the agent slug line, and the proof slider.
social_card.content: The slider pair is real (owner's decision 2026-09-30): the install card as drawn in the design export beside the live CopyBlock built from it, staged at the card's 545px design width and zoomed to fit the 440px pane.

component_sheet.note: The sheet's 'Registration target (mark)' crosshair is the RegistrationTarget atom, a print device, not the logo. The logo is the P mark family (strategy D5), shown in Storybook's Brand story.

scaffold.shared: One SvelteKit app in site/ serves web-desktop and web-mobile; both scaffold gates passed from the same run. Goldens are captured per platform at 1440px and 390px.
scaffold.theme: src/app.css — the only stylesheet (styling contract). Colours are written once with light-dark(); color-scheme follows the system until the toggle sets data-theme on <html> (src/app.html applies a saved choice before first paint). A block-form dark variant covers both the toggle and the no-JS system case. Tailwind's default palette is removed (--color-*: initial).
scaffold.token_names: Decided at scaffold (semantic-colour check): surfaces keep their print names (paper, sheet, ink, muted, line, stripe); the four inks are plates (plate-cyan, plate-cyan-ink, plate-magenta, plate-magenta-ink, plate-yellow) for plate effects and the colour strip only; interaction uses roles: accent (plate-magenta), accent-text (plate-magenta-ink), on-accent (was mark-fg), focus (plate-magenta-ink). Code-panel, drift, and shadow tokens keep their names.
scaffold.fonts: Self-hosted Fontsource packages imported in app.css: @fontsource-variable/anybody (wdth.css, width 50-150%), @fontsource-variable/libre-franklin, @fontsource/ibm-plex-mono 400 and 500.
scaffold.sandbox: npm run sandbox (Storybook on :6006). Stories: Design System/Colors, Typography, Spacing; Components/HelloWorld (scaffold reference, not part of the landing).
scaffold.capture: npm run sandbox:capture builds Storybook, renders every story in light and dark, and writes normalized DOM with each element's resolved colours and type (the golden) plus a PNG (review). Proven stable run to run; a one-token change drifts exactly the stories that use it.
scaffold.color_gate: passed 2026-09-30 (user checked Design System/Colors in both themes)
